transcript.text: Mr. Lincoln. Representative Douglas has brought formal charges that you voted in favor of the Sangamon County land grant while simultaneously representing the principal beneficiary of that grant in your law practice. The ethics of this chamber require that no member profit from legislation he has a hand in passing. You are well-regarded here, sir, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your concern, Representative. However, I assure you that my actions were guided by a commitment to uphold the law and serve the interests of the people. As a lawyer, it is my duty to represent my clients and ensure their rights are protected. The land grant in question was granted to the Illinois Central Railroad Company, which was intended to spur economic growth and development in the region. My representation of the company was not motivated by personal gain, but rather by a belief in the potential benefits it would bring to the state. If you find any impropriety in my actions, please do not hesitate to inform me so that I can rectify the situation if necessary. I am here to serve the people of Illinois, and I will always strive to do so with integrity and impartiality. Thank you for bringing this matter to my attention. I am willing to discuss it further and provide any clarification or explanation that may be required. Let us proceed with a fair and open hearing, and together we can address any concerns that may arise. Thank you, Mr. Speaker.

transcript.text:

Did you, or did you not, represent the Illinois Central Railroad Company at the time of the vote on the Sangamon County land grant? And did you, or did you not, receive payment for that representation? We must understand the exact nature of your involvement, sir.
